verdict.rationale: Jules documents an end-to-end flow: it clones the repo into a VM, installs dependencies, proposes a plan for approval, modifies files, shows a diff and opens a PR (jules-docs-3, -4, -7, -8). Hands-on users report usable PRs (jules-comm-6, jules-comm-16) and say it is good at writing tests for isolated functions (jules-comm-11). Other users report reliability limits, such as tasks not finishing in time (jules-comm-3), weak output beyond simple problems (jules-comm-9) and repeated fixing needed (jules-comm-8), which lowers quality but does not concretely contradict the capability. Missing for 10: first-party documentation that Jules writes or runs tests as part of a feature task, and consistent evidence of reliability on complex, multi-part features.
